title: Graph Modeling & Provenance
description: Study entities, relations and properties, evidence-backed graph assertions, entity resolution and aliases, and temporal facts and graph versions. Each lesson includes a worked example and an applied practice task.

lessons.title: Entities, relations and properties
lessons.description: Write a schema with example nodes, directed edges and required properties.
lessons.conceptOverview: A graph schema defines entity types, relation meanings and properties. Make direction and identity explicit; a relation label without a clear definition encourages inconsistent extraction and unreliable traversal.
lessons.whyItMatters: Consistent relation semantics are necessary for meaningful traversal.

lessons.title: Evidence-backed graph assertions
lessons.description: Design an assertion record that preserves both sources.
lessons.conceptOverview: An extracted edge is a claim supported by a source, not automatically a verified fact. Store source spans, extraction version and confidence so answers can cite evidence and conflicts can be reviewed.
lessons.whyItMatters: Graph assertions should retain evidence and conflicting claims.

lessons.title: Entity resolution and aliases
lessons.description: Define matching evidence and a manual-review threshold.
lessons.conceptOverview: Resolution decides whether mentions refer to the same entity using identifiers and contextual evidence. Aggressive merging creates false links; conservative separation misses connections. Evaluate both error types.
lessons.whyItMatters: Shared names alone do not establish entity identity.

lessons.title: Temporal facts and graph versions
lessons.description: Model valid-from, valid-to and observed-at fields.
lessons.conceptOverview: Relations can change over time. Represent validity periods separately from ingestion time and evaluate queries against the intended date, retaining historical evidence when required.
lessons.whyItMatters: Historical queries require temporal validity, not just current edges.
